raw_response:
I am 76 years old and have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. I finished high school, so I read the fertilizer labels myself and keep notes on what works. Our soil here is loamy and slightly alkaline. I divide the land into 6 mu for wheat-maize double cropping and 2 mu for cotton — the same layout as last year. My son works off-farm in Handan, so labor is just me and my wife, and that limits how much cotton I can pick by hand.

For the winter wheat already in the ground since last October, my basal fertilizer was 50 jin per mu of compound fertilizer at sowing. This spring I will top-dress 20 jin of urea at green-up and another 20 jin at jointing, which gives me about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate four times from the well: overwinter, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I never skip the jointing water — that is when the yield is made. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide at green-up and fungicide at heading. If the spring does not dry out too badly, I expect 520 kg per mu.

Right after wheat harvest in early June, I seed hybrid maize with a no-till machine directly into the wheat stubble. I put 30 jin per mu of compound fertilizer with the seed, then side-dress 25 jin of urea at the big trumpet stage. That totals 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. Maize gets three irrigations — seeding if it is dry, big trumpet, and filling — and two pesticide sprays: pre-emergence herbicide and one for corn borer. I target 600 kg per mu.

For the 2 mu of cotton, I rotary-till in late April and plant Bt hybrid seed. The basal is 40 jin of compound fertilizer plus 20 jin of potassium sulfate per mu, then 15 jin of urea at flowering and another 15 jin at boll stage. Total nutrients work out to 12 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. Three irrigations — seedling, flowering, and peak boll — and three pesticide sprays for aphids and spider mites. I hope for 250 kg per mu of seed cotton.

My fertilizer bill this year will be about 1,800 yuan. That is real money, but last year my neighbor Lao Wang cut back his nitrogen and lost nearly 100 kg per mu on wheat. A bad harvest means I cannot help pay my grandson's school fees. I would rather spend an extra 200 yuan on fertilizer than risk that. Because my budget is tight, I do my own spraying and avoid hired labor except at harvest time.
